purpose: Classify files that are safe for the public/cloud repo versus files that must stay on the operator machine.

cloudSafe.principle: Tracked files may be source code, public docs, sanitized metrics, placeholder config, generated app assets, and reproducible manifests.

localOnly.principle: Secrets, private runtime state, raw operator proof, personal worktrees, generated research sessions, private media, and key material stay local.

trackedDenyPatterns.reason: Contains real operator token and provider keys.
Machine-specific environment files can contain real credentials.
Runtime environment values must stay local unless represented as placeholders in .env.example.
Production environment values must stay local unless represented as placeholders in .env.example.
Test secrets or host values must stay local unless represented as placeholders in .env.example.
Private backups, runtime state, local acceleration vectors, and recovery bundles are host-local.
Replay/recovery checkouts can contain stale env files and old build artifacts.
Temporary push bundles are local operator artifacts.
Temporary runtime output is not repo source.
Local media/library state can contain private titles, links, and operator metadata.
Encrypted private state still belongs to local recovery, not public git.
Private media covers and intake assets stay local.
Phone/iPad acceptance receipts are local proof artifacts.
Raw GitHub export metadata stays local; only sanitized audit summaries are cloud-safe.
Generated research notebooks, provenance sidecars, previews, and PDFs are local working artifacts.
Temporary research scratch output is local-only.
Raw asset intake is not cloud-safe until license, provenance, and manifest checks pass.
Intermediate asset work files are not cloud-safe until normalized and manifest-tracked.
Certificate/private key material must never be tracked.
Key material must never be tracked.
Certificate bundle material must never be tracked.
Certificate bundle material must never be tracked.
Logs can contain local paths, tokens, hostnames, and runtime details.
